patches.name: Layer Info
patches.summary: Reads a layer's size, position, scale, anchor, and parent as they were laid out on the previous frame.
patches.docs:
## How it works
Layer Info reports a layer's real geometry after layout, so you can build on measurements instead of typed numbers. It's how you learn the size of a layer whose width or height is Auto, Grow, or Percent.

- **Layer** is the layer to read.
- **Size** is the width and height in points after layout, before Scale.
- **Position** is where the layer's anchor point sits, in points from its parent's top-left corner.
- **Scale** and **Anchor** are the layer's current values, even while an animation drives them.
- **Enabled** is true while the layer's own Enabled is on.
- **Parent** is the group the layer sits in. Wire it into another Layer Info to measure that group.
- **Content Size** (advanced) is the area a group's children cover.

Every output describes the **previous frame**. Layout runs after patches, so a change shows up here one frame later, about 17 ms at 60 fps.

## Tips
- Hug a text label with a background: add padding to the label's Size and wire the sum into the background's Size.
- To find where a layer sits on screen, or inside another group, use Convert Position.
- Point Layer at a looped layer to get one set of outputs per copy.

## Coming from Origami
- Position is measured from the parent's top-left corner, not its center.
- Content Size is new. When a layer's X and Y scale differ, Scale reports the X factor.

inputs.name: Layer
inputs.description: The layer to read. Leave it empty and every output stays at its empty value.

outputs.name: Size
outputs.description: Width and height in points after layout, not counting Scale (previous frame).

outputs.name: Position
outputs.description: Where the layer's anchor point sits after layout, in points from its parent's top-left corner (previous frame).

outputs.name: Scale
outputs.description: The layer's own scale, not counting its parents' (previous frame); 1 when the layer is missing.

outputs.name: Anchor
outputs.description: Which point of the layer Position refers to, from [0, 0] top-left to [1, 1] bottom-right (previous frame).

outputs.name: Enabled
outputs.description: True while the layer's own Enabled is on (previous frame); false when the layer is missing.

outputs.name: Parent
outputs.description: The group this layer sits in, or empty for a top-level layer; wire it into another Layer Info to measure that group.

outputs.name: Content Size
outputs.description: The area a group's children cover, in points from its top-left corner; [0, 0] when it has no children (previous frame).

commonMistakes: The layer keeps growing every frame: its Size is wired from its own Layer Info plus padding, so each frame adds the padding again. Measure a different layer, such as the text inside, and size the background from that.
Size reads 0 × 0: Layer is empty, or the layer was deleted or sits past the end of its loop. Pick the layer again in the Layer input.
Size doesn't follow a scale animation: Size is the laid-out size before Scale. Multiply Size by Scale when you need the drawn size.

examples.title: Hug a text label with a pill
examples.description: The Text layer sizes itself to its words; the pill adds 16 points of padding on each side and 8 on top and bottom.
examples.outline:
layer pill rectangle "Pill" @16,96 size←pill_size.output cornerRadius=18 color=#1F6FEBFF
layer label text "Label" "3 new messages" @32,104 textColor=#FFFFFFFF
patch label_info layerInfo layer=@label
patch pill_size add<size>[2] value1←label_info.size value2=[32,16]

examples.title: Fill a progress bar to a track of any width
examples.description: The track is 92% of the screen wide on every device. Tap anywhere to fill it; the fill's final size comes from the track's measured size.
examples.outline:
layer track rectangle "Track" @16,420 92x8 widthMode=percent cornerRadius=4 color=#E5E5EAFF
layer fill rectangle "Fill" @16,420 size←fill_size.output cornerRadius=4 color=#34C759FF
patch track_info layerInfo layer=@track
patch tap_anywhere interaction
patch loaded switch flip←tap_anywhere.tap
patch fill_anim classicAnimation number←loaded.on duration=2
patch fill_size transition<size> progress←fill_anim.output start=[0,8] end←track_info.size

patches.name: Convert Position
patches.summary: Converts a point from one layer's coordinate space to another's, so a layer can line up with a layer in a different group.
patches.docs:
## How it works
Every layer measures positions from its parent's top-left corner, so one spot on screen has different coordinates inside different groups. Convert Position translates a point from one layer's space into another's. It accounts for scrolling, scale, and layout.

- **From Layer** is the layer the point belongs to. Leave it empty to start from screen coordinates.
- **Position** is the point, in points from From Layer's **Anchor**. With both at [0, 0] it's the layer's top-left corner.
- **To Layer** is the layer whose space you want the answer in, usually the **parent** of the layer you're moving. Leave it empty for screen coordinates.
- **To Anchor** measures the answer from another point of To Layer: [0.5, 0.5] gives the offset from its center.
- **Converted Position** is the answer. **Error** turns on when a layer can't be found.

Like Layer Info, it reads the layout of the previous frame.

## Tips
- Make layer B follow layer A: set From Layer to A and To Layer to B's parent, then wire Converted Position into B's Position.
- Set Anchor to where B should attach: [1, 0] is A's top-right corner. Give B an Anchor of [0.5, 0.5] to center it on that spot.

## Coming from Origami
From Parent and To Parent are called From Layer and To Layer, the unnamed input is Position, and coordinates start at the top-left. Disabled layers still convert: Error means a layer is missing.

inputs.name: From Layer
inputs.description: The layer the point belongs to. Leave it empty to start from screen coordinates.

inputs.name: Position
inputs.description: The point to convert, in points from From Layer's Anchor; [0, 0] is the anchor point itself.

inputs.name: Anchor
inputs.description: Which point of From Layer Position is measured from: [0, 0] top-left, [0.5, 0.5] center, [1, 1] bottom-right.

inputs.name: To Layer
inputs.description: The layer whose space you want the answer in, usually the parent of the layer you're moving; empty means screen coordinates.

inputs.name: To Anchor
inputs.description: Measures the answer from this point of To Layer: [0, 0] its top-left, [0.5, 0.5] its center.

outputs.name: Converted Position
outputs.description: The point in To Layer's space, measured from To Anchor, from the previous frame's layout; wire it into the Position of a child of To Layer.

outputs.name: Error
outputs.description: True when a layer can't be found or To Layer is scaled to 0; Converted Position then holds its last good value.

commonMistakes: The badge jitters or drifts away: To Layer is the badge itself, so every move changes the space it's measured in. Set To Layer to the badge's parent, or leave it empty when the badge sits directly on the screen.

The follower sits half a layer off: the follower's own Anchor doesn't match the spot you attach to. Set Anchor to that spot on From Layer, and give the follower an Anchor of [0.5, 0.5] when it should be centered there.
The overlay trails a frame behind while scrolling: positions come from the previous frame's layout. When the overlay must move exactly with the content, put it inside the scrolling group instead.

examples.title: Pin a badge to a card that scrolls
examples.description: The badge lives outside the feed, so the feed's clipping can't cut it off. With To Layer empty, the answer is in screen coordinates, which is the badge's parent space.
examples.outline:
layer feed group "Feed" @0,0 402x874 clip=true
  layer list group "List" 402x2000 position←feed_scroll.position
    layer card rectangle "Card" @16,300 370x200 cornerRadius=20
layer badge oval "Badge" 28x28 anchor=[0.5,0.5] position←pin.convertedPosition color=#FF3B30FF
patch feed_scroll scroll layer=@list
patch pin convertPosition fromLayer=@card anchor=[1,0]

examples.title: Grow a photo out of its thumbnail
examples.description: Convert Position finds the thumbnail on screen, so the full-size photo starts exactly on top of it wherever the gallery sits.
examples.outline:
layer gallery group "Gallery" @0,160 402x600
  layer thumb image "Thumb" @136,80 130x130 cornerRadius=12
layer viewer image "Viewer" position←grow_position.output size←grow_size.output opacity←open_anim.output
patch tap_thumb interaction layer=@thumb
patch tap_viewer interaction layer=@viewer
patch open switch turnOn←tap_thumb.tap turnOff←tap_viewer.tap
patch open_anim popAnimation number←open.on bounciness=2 speed=14
patch thumb_spot convertPosition fromLayer=@thumb
patch grow_position transition<point> progress←open_anim.output start←thumb_spot.convertedPosition end=[0,0]
patch grow_size transition<size> progress←open_anim.output start=[130,130] end=[402,874]

defaultNotes.position: inferred: the docs suggest 0,0 as the usual starting point but state no default.
defaultNotes.anchor: sonobe: Origami's default is unpublished; top-left matches Sonobe's default layer Anchor.
defaultNotes.toLayer: inferred: the docs show None; reading an empty To Layer as screen coordinates follows the research's reading of the algorithm.
defaultNotes.toAnchor: sonobe: top-left, so the answer can drive a child layer's Position directly.

patches.name: Blur Effect
patches.summary: Creates a blur for a layer's Effects property, softening everything the layer draws, with an option to keep its edges sharp.
patches.docs:
## How it works
Blur Effect makes an effect value: a description of a visual effect a layer applies to itself. Wire **Effect** into a layer's **Effects** property, in the Filters section of the inspector, and the layer and its children look out of focus.

- **Radius** is how strong the blur is, in points. 0 turns it off.
- **Hard Edges** keeps the layer's outline crisp and opaque instead of letting the blur fade out past its edges. Turn it on for full-bleed photos and backgrounds.

To apply several effects to one layer, collect them in a Loop Builder and wire its loop into Effects. They apply in order.

## Tips
- Animate Radius with a Transition to pull focus, for example to blur the page while a menu opens.
- A Radius of 20 to 30 gives a soft backdrop behind menus and sheets; 2 to 6 reads as slightly out of focus.
- For a different blur on each copy of a looped layer, drive the layer's Blur property instead. Effects applies a loop of effects to every copy.

## Coming from Origami
The output is called Effect instead of Layer Effect. Radius uses the same scale as the layer's Blur property.
patches.behavior:
Stateless.

Each frame:
```
let radius = ctx.input("radius");
if (!Number.isFinite(radius)) { warnOnce("Blur Effect: Radius isn't a finite number; using 0."); radius = 0; }
ctx.output("effect", {
  kind: "blur",
  params: { radius: Math.max(0, radius), hardEdges: ctx.input("hardEdges") },
});
```

- Value: a `LayerEffectValue` with kind `"blur"` and params `radius` (points, ≥ 0) and `hardEdges` (boolean). The patch outputs an effect object even at radius 0, so loop indices stay stable; renderers skip no-op effects.
- Rendering (renderer contract): a layer's Effects apply in loop order, after the layer's own Blur property and before its drop shadow, to the layer's composited content including children. Radius is the Gaussian standard deviation in points, the same scale as the layer's Blur property (CSS `blur(<radius>px)`).
  - Hard Edges off: pixels outside the layer's bounds count as transparent, so the silhouette softens and bleeds outward by about 3 × Radius.
  - Hard Edges on: pixels outside the bounds count as copies of the nearest edge pixel, and the result is clipped to the layer's shape (corner radius and smoothing included), so edges stay sharp and opaque. Preferred web approach: an SVG `feGaussianBlur` with `edgeMode="duplicate"` plus a clip to the layer's shape. Where a browser ignores `edgeMode`, clip only; a thin band inside the edge may look slightly darker. (The DOM renderer's `effectFilters` doesn't read `hardEdges` yet.)
- Frame 0: outputs the effect for the authored values; nothing animates.
- Loops: per-index evaluation gives a loop of effects. A layer's Effects property takes whole loops (`wholeLoop: true` in layerTypes.ts), so wiring that loop stacks every effect on the layer, and on every copy of a looped layer.
- Edge cases: a negative Radius becomes 0; NaN or ±Infinity becomes 0 with one warning per restart through `ctx.services.log("warn", …)`. There's no upper clamp; renderers may cap very large radii for performance.
- Muted: default bypass. Effect has no matching input and outputs null, so the layer shows no effect.
- Platform and simulation: CSS filters work in the desktop app and every supported browser. Headless simulation carries the value in `SceneNode.props.effects` without drawing it.
- Restart and dispose: nothing to reset.
- Coming from Origami: `builtin.blurLayerEffect`, library category Layer Effects, ports Radius → Layer Effect (gap-fill §4.3). Hard Edges arrived later under an unpublished label; importers map it by name when present. Origami's radius units are unpublished; Sonobe uses the CSS standard deviation.

inputs.name: Radius
inputs.description: How strong the blur is, in points; 0 turns it off, and larger values look more out of focus.

inputs.name: Hard Edges
inputs.description: When on, the layer's edges stay sharp and opaque instead of fading out past its bounds.

outputs.name: Effect
outputs.description: Wire into a layer's Effects property to blur that layer.

commonMistakes: Nothing blurs: Effect isn't wired into the layer's Effects property, or it's wired into a different layer. Open the layer's Filters section and connect Effect to Effects.
The photo's edges look faded and see-through: without Hard Edges, the blur pulls in transparent pixels from outside the layer. Turn on Hard Edges for full-bleed images and backgrounds.
The panel's own text blurs instead of what's behind it: Blur Effect blurs the layer's own content. To frost what's behind a panel, use the panel's Background Blur property or Glass Effect.

examples.title: Blur the page while a menu is held open
examples.description: A long press opens the menu, and the same animation drives the blur, so both move together.
examples.outline:
layer photo image "Photo" @0,0 402x874 effects←background_blur.effect
layer menu rectangle "Menu" @101,357 200x160 cornerRadius=16 color=#FFFFFFFF opacity←menu_anim.output
patch hold longPress layer=@photo
patch menu_anim popAnimation number←hold.longPress bounciness=3 speed=16
patch blur_amount transition<number> progress←menu_anim.output start=0 end=20
patch background_blur blurEffect radius←blur_amount.output hardEdges=true

examples.title: Stack a soft blur with a dimmed tone
examples.description: A Loop Builder collects both effects, and the layer applies them in order.
examples.outline:
layer hero image "Hero" @0,0 402x320 effects←stack.loop
patch soft blurEffect radius=6 hardEdges=true
patch dim colorControlsEffect brightness=-0.2 saturation=0.6
patch stack loopBuilder<layerEffect>[2] item0←soft.effect item1←dim.effect

defaultNotes.radius: sonobe: Origami's default is unpublished (research guesses 0 or 10); 10 shows the blur as soon as it's connected.
defaultNotes.hardEdges: inferred: Hard Edges was added later as an option, so off matches the original look.

patches.name: Color Controls Effect
patches.summary: Adjusts a layer's brightness, contrast, saturation, and hue through its Effects property.
patches.docs:
## How it works
Color Controls Effect makes an effect value that shifts a layer's colors. Wire **Effect** into a layer's **Effects** property and the layer, including its children, changes tone. Every control starts at a neutral value that leaves the layer unchanged.

- **Brightness** lightens or darkens: 0 is unchanged, −1 is black, and 1 is twice as bright.
- **Contrast** spreads colors apart: 1 is unchanged, 0 is flat gray, and 2 doubles the contrast.
- **Saturation** sets how vivid colors are: 1 is unchanged, 0 is black and white, and 2 is twice as vivid.
- **Hue Rotation** turns every color around the color wheel, in degrees. 180 swaps colors for their opposites.

## Tips
- Gray out a disabled card: Saturation 0 and Brightness 0.1.
- Animate one control with a Transition and leave the others at their neutral values.
- Combine it with Blur Effect by collecting both in a Loop Builder wired into Effects.

inputs.name: Brightness
inputs.description: Lightens or darkens the layer: 0 is unchanged, −1 is black, and 1 is twice as bright.

inputs.name: Contrast
inputs.description: Spreads colors apart: 1 is unchanged, 0 is flat gray, and 2 doubles the contrast.

inputs.name: Saturation
inputs.description: How vivid colors are: 1 is unchanged, 0 is black and white, and 2 is twice as vivid.

inputs.name: Hue Rotation
inputs.description: Turns every color around the color wheel, in degrees; 0 is unchanged and 180 gives opposite colors.

outputs.name: Effect
outputs.description: Wire into a layer's Effects property to recolor that layer.

commonMistakes: The layer turns gray as soon as you connect it: Saturation or Contrast is at 0. Their neutral value is 1; only Brightness and Hue Rotation are neutral at 0.
The label and icons on a card change color too: effects apply to the whole layer, children included. Apply the effect to the photo layer instead of the group that holds everything.

examples.title: Bring a photo to color when tapped
examples.outline:
layer photo image "Photo" @16,140 370x370 cornerRadius=20 effects←tone.effect
patch tap_photo interaction layer=@photo
patch revealed switch flip←tap_photo.tap
patch reveal_anim classicAnimation number←revealed.on duration=0.6
patch vividness transition<number> progress←reveal_anim.output start=0 end=1
patch tone colorControlsEffect saturation←vividness.output

examples.title: Brighten a thumbnail on hover
examples.description: One spring drives both controls, so brightness and contrast rise together while the pointer is over the thumbnail.
examples.outline:
layer thumb image "Thumb" @136,300 130x130 cornerRadius=12 effects←hover_tone.effect
patch hover_thumb hover layer=@thumb
patch lift popAnimation number←hover_thumb.hovering bounciness=2 speed=18
patch lighten transition<number> progress←lift.output start=0 end=0.15
patch punch transition<number> progress←lift.output start=1 end=1.1
patch hover_tone colorControlsEffect brightness←lighten.output contrast←punch.output

defaultNotes.brightness: sonobe: neutral, so the effect changes only the controls you adjust.
defaultNotes.contrast: sonobe: neutral (1), so the effect changes only the controls you adjust.
defaultNotes.saturation: sonobe: neutral (1), so the effect changes only the controls you adjust.
defaultNotes.hueRotation: sonobe: neutral, so the effect changes only the controls you adjust.

patches.name: Glass Effect
patches.statusReason: The frosted blur, tint, and rim work everywhere through CSS backdrop-filter. Refraction needs an SVG filter inside backdrop-filter, which only Chromium supports, so Safari and Firefox show the glass without lensing.
patches.summary: Turns a layer into a pane of glass that frosts, tints, and bends whatever sits behind it, with a bright rim along its edge.
patches.docs:
## How it works
Glass Effect makes an effect value that turns a layer into a glass pane. Wire **Effect** into a layer's **Effects** property: whatever is behind the layer shows through frosted and tinted, bent near the edges like a lens, with a light rim. The pane follows the layer's shape, including corner radius and smoothing.

- **Intensity** fades the whole effect: 0 is no glass, 1 is full glass. Animate it to bring glass in or out.
- **Frost** is how much the background blurs, in points.
- **Tint** is a color washed over the glass; its alpha sets how strong it is.
- **Refraction** is how strongly the edges bend what's behind, from 0 to 1.
- **Highlight** is how bright the rim light is, from 0 to 1.
- **Saturation** and **Depth** (advanced) boost background colors and set how far the lens reaches in from the edge.

Children of the layer draw on top of the glass, sharp and unaffected.

## Tips
- Clear glass over photos: Frost 2, a Tint alpha around 5%, and Refraction 0.8.
- Match the theme: choose a dark Tint in dark mode with Device Info and If / Else.
- Glass is expensive to draw. On phones, use a few panes rather than a grid of them.

## Coming from Origami
Origami's glass support has unpublished parameters. This patch is Sonobe's own design, and imported glass doesn't carry its settings over.
patches.behavior:
Stateless.

Each frame:
```
const k = clamp01(finiteOr(ctx.input("intensity"), 1));
const tint = ctx.input("tint");                                   // Color { r, g, b, a }
const saturation = Math.max(0, finiteOr(ctx.input("saturation"), 1));
ctx.output("effect", {
  kind: "glass",
  params: {
    frost: Math.max(0, finiteOr(ctx.input("frost"), 0)) * k,
    tint: { r: tint.r, g: tint.g, b: tint.b, a: tint.a * k },
    refraction: clamp01(finiteOr(ctx.input("refraction"), 0)) * k,
    highlight: clamp01(finiteOr(ctx.input("highlight"), 0)) * k,
    saturation: 1 + (saturation - 1) * k,
    depth: Math.max(0, finiteOr(ctx.input("depth"), 0)),
  },
});
```
`finiteOr(v, neutral)` returns `neutral` for NaN or ±Infinity and warns once per restart through `ctx.services.log("warn", …)`.

- Value: a `LayerEffectValue` with kind `"glass"` and params `frost`, `tint`, `refraction`, `highlight`, `saturation`, and `depth`. Intensity is folded into the params, so renderers never see it: at Intensity 0 every param is neutral and the effect is a no-op.
- Rendering (renderer contract; the DOM renderer's `effectFilters` has no `"glass"` case yet). Clip every step to the layer's shape (Corner Radius, Corner Radii, Corner Smoothing, or the oval):
  1. Backdrop: sample the composited content behind the layer in z-order (earlier siblings, ancestors' backgrounds, and everything below), never the layer's own content or children.
  2. Refraction: for a pixel at distance `e` points inside the nearest shape edge with `e < depth`, sample the backdrop at `pixel + n × refraction × depth × (1 − e / depth)²`, where `n` is that edge's outward unit normal, so the rim shows content from slightly beyond the pane. Deeper pixels sample straight behind themselves. Skip when refraction or depth is 0.
  3. Frost: Gaussian blur of the displaced backdrop with standard deviation `frost` points, then the CSS `saturate(saturation)` matrix.
  4. Tint: composite `tint` source-over.
  5. Highlight: a white rim 1.5 pt wide inside the edge, with alpha `highlight × (0.25 + 0.75 × max(0, n · (−0.7071, −0.7071)))`, brightest on edges facing up and left.
  6. Draw the layer's own fill, stroke, and children on top.

  If a layer's Effects loop holds several glass effects, only the last one applies. Blur and color effects in the same loop still filter the layer's own content.
- DOM approach: `backdrop-filter: [url(#lens)] blur(<frost>px) saturate(<saturation>)` with the `-webkit-` prefix, the tint as a background under the layer's fill, and the rim as an SVG stroke or an inset box-shadow. The lens is an SVG `feDisplacementMap` fed by a generated edge-distance map, used only where `backdrop-filter: url()` works (Chromium, including Electron).
- Frame 0: outputs the effect for the authored values.
- Loops: per-index evaluation gives a loop of effects. A layer's Effects property takes whole loops (see Blur Effect).
- Edge cases: Intensity, Refraction, and Highlight clamp to 0–1; a negative Frost, Depth, or Saturation becomes 0; NaN or ±Infinity uses the neutral value (Intensity and Saturation 1, others 0). A layer with zero size draws nothing.
- Muted: default bypass. Effect outputs null and the layer shows no glass.
- Platform and simulation: backdrop blur, saturation, tint, and rim work in the desktop app and in current Chromium, Safari, and Firefox. Lensing is Chromium-only; elsewhere step 2 is skipped. On the web, an ancestor with opacity below 1, a blend mode, a filter, or effects of its own limits the backdrop to that ancestor's contents. Headless simulation carries the value in `SceneNode.props.effects` and draws nothing.
- Restart and dispose: nothing to reset. The renderer releases generated SVG filters when the layer is removed.
- Coming from Origami: Origami added glass support with unpublished parameters (census row "Liquid Glass"). This spec is a clean-room design; imported files keep the wiring but not the parameters.

inputs.name: Intensity
inputs.description: Fades the whole effect: 0 is no glass and 1 is full glass.

inputs.name: Frost
inputs.description: How much what's behind the glass blurs, in points; 0 keeps it sharp.

inputs.name: Tint
inputs.description: A color washed over the glass; its alpha sets the strength, and an alpha of 0 means no tint.

inputs.name: Refraction
inputs.description: How strongly the edges bend what's behind, like a lens: 0 is flat and 1 is strongest.

inputs.name: Highlight
inputs.description: How bright the light rim along the edge is, brightest at the top left; 0 turns it off.

inputs.name: Saturation
inputs.description: Boosts the colors seen through the glass: 1 is unchanged and 0 is black and white.

inputs.name: Depth
inputs.description: How far the lens bending reaches in from the edge, in points; 0 turns refraction off.

outputs.name: Effect
outputs.description: Wire into a layer's Effects property to turn that layer into glass.

commonMistakes: The glass looks like a flat gray panel: the layer's Color is opaque and covers the glass. Set the layer's Color alpha to 0 and use Tint for color.
Nothing shows through the glass: the content is in front of the glass layer, not behind it. Glass only shows layers below it in the layer list, so move the glass layer above the content.
The glass frosts its own label: the label is a sibling behind the glass. Make the label a child of the glass layer so it draws on top, sharp.

examples.title: A glass tab bar over a scrolling feed
examples.description: The feed scrolls under the bar, and the label inside the bar stays sharp on top of the glass.
examples.outline:
layer feed group "Feed" 402x2400 position←feed_scroll.position
layer tab_bar group "Tab Bar" @24,780 354x64 cornerRadius=32 cornerSmoothing=0.6 effects←bar_glass.effect
  layer home_label text "Home" "Home" @40,22
patch feed_scroll scroll layer=@feed
patch bar_glass glassEffect frost=10 tint=#FFFFFF33 refraction=0.6

examples.title: Turn a header to glass once content scrolls under it
examples.description: The header is clear at the top of the page and becomes full glass after 80 points of scrolling.
examples.outline:
layer feed group "Feed" 402x2400 position←feed_scroll.position
layer header group "Header" @0,0 402x96 effects←header_glass.effect
  layer title text "Title" "Library" @16,56
patch feed_scroll scroll layer=@feed
patch scrolled progress value←feed_scroll.y start=0 end=-80 clampToRange=true
patch header_glass glassEffect intensity←scrolled.progress frost=12 refraction=0.3

defaultNotes.intensity: sonobe: full glass as soon as it's connected.
defaultNotes.frost: sonobe: Origami's parameters are unpublished; 8 pt clearly frosts while keeping background shapes readable.
defaultNotes.tint: sonobe: a 15% white wash reads as glass over both light and dark content.
defaultNotes.refraction: sonobe: a visible lens at the rim that leaves the middle undistorted.
defaultNotes.highlight: sonobe: a noticeable rim that doesn't read as a border.
defaultNotes.saturation: sonobe: a mild boost keeps colors behind the glass from looking washed out.
defaultNotes.depth: sonobe: 16 pt suits typical button and bar sizes.
